Automotive and EV
Body control, battery management, motor control, infotainment, driver-assistance support. CAN bus and, later, AUTOSAR and functional safety (ISO 26262) matter here.
Tier-1 suppliers and engineering-services firms such as Bosch, Continental, KPIT and Tata Elxsi are named in one salary guide.
Global capability centres and chip companies
Firmware, board support packages, drivers and validation for products designed for a parent company abroad.
Qualcomm, Texas Instruments, Bosch and Intel appear in the salary guides we read. Check live openings for current lists.
Industrial, IoT and smart-meter products
Gateways, sensors, controllers and meters. Often a small team where one engineer covers hardware, firmware and testing.
Indian product firms and startups. Names change often, so use job listings, not a fixed list.
Medical devices
Monitors, pumps, diagnostic instruments. Slow release cycles, heavy documentation, strict safety rules.
Check the company page for each opening.
Defence, space and public research
Avionics, communication and control electronics through labs and public-sector units. Hired through exams and notices.
ISRO, DRDO and public-sector units post their own notices.

blocks.heading: Rung By Rung
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: The skills ladder, rung by rung

rows: 1. C and a real microcontroller
C (pointers, bit operations, memory), a board such as an ARM Cortex-M development board, GPIO, timers, interrupts.
A small project written without a code-generating wizard doing all the work, with a short README.
2. Protocols and measuring tools
UART, I2C, SPI, CAN; reading a datasheet; a logic analyser and a multimeter.
A capture or photo that shows a sensor talking to your board, plus one note on a bug you found.
3. RTOS and Linux
FreeRTOS or Zephyr tasks, queues, priorities; Linux basics, cross-compiling, device drivers or a small board such as a Raspberry Pi class computer.
A multi-task project with a plain explanation of why you chose each priority.
4. Quality and safety habits
Unit tests on firmware, static analysis, MISRA-C rules, version control discipline, simple hardware-in-the-loop testing.
A repository with tests and a pass report that someone else can run.
5. A domain
One sector in depth: automotive buses and safety, battery systems, medical rules, wireless, or industrial control.
A project that matches the sector, reviewed by someone who works in it.

blocks.heading: Embedded, VLSI, Robotics or Mechatronics
rows: Embedded Firmware
Best-Balanced Start for Most ECE, EEE and Instrumentation Students.
Scalable with a Business Layer
Embedded Firmware
Best-Balanced Start for Most ECE, EEE and Instrumentation Students.
Scalable with a Business Layer
Embedded firmware
Code that runs on devices. Needs C, a board and patience with debugging.
Broad. Many sectors, many company sizes. One guide says someone with good C and basic microcontroller knowledge can become productive fairly quickly.
VLSI: design verification
Building testbenches that try to break a chip design before it is made. Uses SystemVerilog, simulators and scripting.
Narrower. Concentrated in semiconductor and chip-design firms. Strong programming helps, and a common path runs from embedded into verification.
VLSI: RTL and physical design
RTL is writing the chip logic in Verilog or VHDL. Physical design is turning that logic into a layout: placement, clock trees, routing, timing closure.
Narrow and tool-heavy. One course provider's comparison says moving from embedded to VLSI means learning hardware description languages and design tools from the start.
Semiconductor fab and packaging
Process, equipment, yield and test work in factories that make or package chips.
Jobs are opening as new plants come up, but these are factory and process roles, not firmware or design roles. Plants are still being built.
Robotics
A robot is embedded control plus mechanics plus software. Most early jobs are in control, automation, vision or integration, not robot design.
University blogs list modest starting ranges that conflict with each other, and note that many robotics titles ask for experience.
Mechatronics
A degree that blends mechanical, electronics and control. The jobs are automation, PLC, embedded, instrumentation and controls.
Employers hire for the skill, so the degree helps only when you can show embedded or PLC work.
VLSI: design verification
Good for people who like finding bugs and writing code. Often a smoother pivot from embedded than design.
Scalable with a business layer
VLSI: RTL and physical design
High reward for strong digital-electronics students who can move to a chip-design city. A hard fit for a student who only likes coding.
Scalable with a business layer
Semiconductor fab and packaging
A different career from embedded. Check the exact role and degree asked.
Not so scalable
Robotics
Reasonable if you add a skill that companies buy now: embedded control, PLC or vision. Weak as a stand-alone degree label.
Scalable with a business layer
Mechatronics
A decent route into automation. If you are choosing between degrees, pick the one whose labs and projects let you build.
Scalable with a business layer
The Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 in July 2026 as a further push for chip making and design in India. Check pib.gov.in for the outlay and unit counts, which sources report differently.
Press Information Bureau (PIB)
Policy support is large and covers design, fabrication, packaging, equipment, materials and talent. It does not set the number of fresher jobs.
12 manufacturing units approved with investment above Rs 1.64 lakh crore. Other tallies say 10 or 13, depending on date and scheme.
PIB; India Briefing (counts differ)
Most of these are plants and packaging units. Their jobs are mostly process, equipment and test roles.
The largest fab project, Tata Electronics at Dholera, is targeted for commercial operations in FY 2029-30. Some packaging units have already opened.
India Briefing, May 2026
The big fab is years away. Plan for roles that exist now, not for a plant that is still being built.
Government programmes train students on chip-design tools across many universities and give startups access to industry design tools. Check the latest PIB release for current counts.
PIB, Semicon 2.0 release
Tool access exists in many colleges. Ask your department what you can use for free before paying a training firm.

blocks.heading: Degree, Diploma or Skills: the Entry Routes
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Degree, diploma or skills: the entry routes

rows: B.Tech in ECE or EEE
The most direct. Digital electronics, microcontroller and signals subjects match the work. Many colleges still run thin labs, so the board work is yours to add.
Own a board by second year and build in public.
Instrumentation or mechatronics degree
Direct for control, automation and embedded-control roles. Add C and one RTOS.
Show an embedded project, not only a PLC lab record.
CSE or IT
Possible, because C and operating-system skills transfer. You will need to add electronics basics: reading circuits and datasheets, and using a scope.
Start with Linux-based boards, then go to bare-metal microcontrollers.
Diploma in electronics or electrical
A real entry for testing, assembly, service and junior firmware tasks. A degree is a common filter for design roles, so plan a bridge such as lateral entry or a strong project record.
Build proof early and read the diploma guide for the bridge options.
Other branches or working professionals
Harder, but not closed. Many people move in from testing, electronics service or software. Employers watch for proof, not branch.
Choose a narrow first target such as board testing or embedded Linux support.

blocks.heading: Who Should Skip Embedded
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Who should skip embedded, or choose another door

rows: You want a job that is mostly coding in a clean, fast cycle
Embedded work includes waiting for hardware, chasing faults that appear once a day, and reading datasheets. If a long debugging session will drain you, choose a software route.
You will not touch a board, a probe or a multimeter
Without hands-on work you become a weaker software applicant who also lacks the hardware edge. Pure coding roles pay the same or more.
You are choosing VLSI only because the chip news is exciting
New plants mostly create process and packaging jobs. Design seats for freshers are limited. Test the work with free tools first.
You want a big salary in the first year without proof
The pay sources disagree widely and none names its data. Offers follow proof, not branch.
You need a lab, a board and tools but cannot afford even a small kit
This is solvable, since boards and free tools are cheap next to a course fee. But plan the small spend first, or begin on a simulator.
